chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he was asked about a man who prayed without purity, or forgot prayers that he did not pray, or slept through them, so he said:

He should make up for it when he remembers it, at whatever hour he remembers it, from night or day. So when the time for the prayer enters and he has not completed what has passed, let him make up for what he does not fear the time of this present prayer will depart, and this is more deserving of its time, so let him pray it. So when he has made it up, let him pray what has passed from what is missed, and he should not offer an optional prayer by even one rak'ah until he has made up the obligatory prayer, all of it.

key_terms.قَضَاء: Making up for missed obligatory acts of worship

ai.seo_question: What is the correct order for making up missed obligatory prayers and when should optional prayers be performed?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the priority of making up missed obligatory prayers (qada) over voluntary ones, emphasizing that one must not perform nafl prayers until all fard prayers are completed. It further specifies the procedure for handling overlapping prayer times, ensuring that the current prayer's time is not missed while catching up on previous ones. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on maintaining the integrity of obligatory worship and the sequential nature of debt repayment in spiritual duties.
